CarDrawer 차서랍

Android app for used-car dealers in Korea

Recruiting 5 pilot shopsClosed testing on Google Play soon

One drawer
per car.

AI files every receipt and flags what's missing.

Snap a receipt, invoice or inspection report, or share a PDF. CarDrawer pulls out the vendor, amount, date and plate as suggestions and files them in that car's drawer. Every morning it shows what is due today, which papers are missing, which costs need approval and which cars have started losing money.

Apply for the pilot How it works

Free cost sheet template (CSV) · A per-car cost sheet that opens in Excel: 18 cost items with total-cost and difference formulas. No sign-up or email needed.

  • AI only suggests. A person confirms.
  • We never ask for your HeyDealer, Encar or other platform passwords.
  • Your costs are visible only to you and the people you allow.
The problem

Costs leak car by car, and papers scatter across chat rooms

Receipts in drawers and chats

Transport, polish, body work, dealer fees, listing ads: one car collects close to ten cost items. Matching each receipt to the right car falls on the office manager.

Deadlines in someone's head

Ownership transfer, inspection-report validity and platform claim windows differ for every car. Missing one means fines or disputes.

Profit known only after the sale

Financing interest and late invoices can turn a car you thought was profitable into a loss, and it is hard to see where each car stands today.

A car bought for ₩30.01M: about ₩630,000 left if sold in 3 months · cut the price in month 7 and it becomes a ₩970,000 loss

A dealer's public cost sheet (9 cost items; re-listing, interest and re-inspection added in month 7). Source: Clien post, 23 Aug 2025 (Korean), checked Oct 2026. One case, not a general figure.
What it does

Snap it, it sticks. Missing pieces come first.

  • Snap and it sticks

    “Snap the receipt. We attach it to the right car.”

    Upload from the camera, gallery or share menu in three taps. AI suggests the vendor, amount, date and plate; only values checked against the original reach your costs.

  • Today's deadlines, cars losing money

    “Do you know how much this car still makes?”

    The first screen gathers overdue tasks, today's deadlines, pending approvals and at-risk cars, with legal, platform and in-house deadlines labelled separately.

  • One shop, your costs stay yours

    “You decide who sees what.”

    Owner, buyers and office staff share the same car cards. Purchase prices, costs and counterparties are visible only with permission, and access ends the moment someone leaves.

  • Works next to your apps

    “Keep your apps. We fill the gaps.”

    Cars from any channel on one board. Platform screenshots are stored, never scraped. Export costs as CSV for your existing system or accountant.

How it works

Upload → suggest → confirm → organise

  1. Upload on the lot. Buyers photograph receipts, invoices and inspection reports or share them. The app asks you to mask resident registration and similar ID numbers yourself with its masking tool before upload, and photo location data is removed on the device.
  2. AI suggests values. It sorts document types and copies vendor, amount, date and plate exactly as written. Fixed formulas, not AI, clean up and check the numbers.
  3. A person confirms against the original. Amounts, the car a document belongs to, odometer, accident or replacement marks and seizure or mortgage status always need human approval. The office can review in one batch later.
  4. Costs, deadlines and sales prep update. Confirmed values fill per-car costs and break-even, paperwork checklists, required ad items and draft descriptions.

“No information” is not “no problem”

Blank never means “none”. Every value carries a state, and anything not confirmed stays out of outgoing material.

  • Confirmed

  • Needs review

Things the app never does for you

  • Post listings, send messages, transfer money, bid or file documents. It prepares files and text and hands them to the share menu.
  • Connect to or scrape other platforms. Platform screenshots and auction diagnoses are stored only, never sent to AI.
  • Declare a car “accident-free” or write “warranty” or “lowest price” without evidence.
  • Perform statutory disclosure, inspections or ownership transfer. Those duties stay with the dealer.
  • Recommend purchase prices. The purchase-limit calculator only uses the assumptions you enter.
  • Give tax advice or file returns. It tags receipts and exports them.
Data and privacy

Customer data belongs to the dealership

  • For owner and buyer details in uploaded records, the dealership is the controller and we process them only as instructed. They are never used for marketing or AI training.
  • Data is stored in Google Cloud's Seoul region. Document reading uses Google Vertex AI (Gemini, paid tier), which may process outside Korea.
  • No advertising SDK or advertising ID. No payments inside the app.
  • Export everything as CSV and an original-file ZIP at any time, and for 30 days after you cancel.

No. We don't take platform credentials or scrape anything. Screenshots or diagnosis files you upload are stored in the car's drawer and never sent to AI.

What if AI reads an amount wrong?

AI values stay marked “AI suggestion” until a person approves them against the original. Amounts and the car a document belongs to always need approval. Use “Report a problem” on any wrong result.

SugarMount is an Android app brand run by simpest, an independent developer, making small apps that each do one job. Ten of them are on Google Play, from a Korean spelling checker and an HWP viewer to photo tools and two puzzle games.

Who makes the apps

SugarMount is the developer name used by simpest, an independent developer, to publish apps on Google Play. Planning, development, releases and support are all done by the same person. It is not a company or a team.

How the apps are built and checked

In their repositories, 195 of 212 commits (92%) carry an AI co-author line (git history, October 18, 2026). SugarSpeller has been updated the same way since August 2025. The agent writes code, tests and release scripts; a person decides ad placement, pricing and releases, and checks on real devices.
  • Release builds run on a device before upload. The three photo apps and HWP Viewer SugarDoc go through a release gate (leftover test ad IDs, empty config, policy URLs), two launches of the shrunk release build, and end-to-end tests on a real device. Details are in the release check note.
  • Policies come from the code. Privacy policies are written after checking each app's source code and SDK settings, and say nothing the code doesn't back.
  • Numbers carry a source and a date. Numbers on this site come from the app repositories' git history, changelogs and device QA reports, with the date they were taken. What we could not verify, we leave out.

The process and the measured numbers are written up in the AX notes.

Principles

  • Photos and documents stay on the device

    The apps that handle photos, videos and documents (Compress Image, Flip & Rotate Image, Convert Image, SugarAlbum, HWP Viewer SugarDoc) process files on the device without uploading them, and never modify or delete the originals.

  • No sign-up

    None of the ten public apps has a sign-up or log-in screen. SugarSpeller creates an anonymous ID, not linked to any name or email, to count daily use of AI explanations.

  • Policies that match the code

    Each app's privacy policy is written from its actual code, including what the ad and analytics SDKs send.

Privacy

What leaves the device differs by app. For example, SugarSpeller sends the text you check to the Naver or Daum (Kakao) spelling checker, while the photo apps send no photos. Each app's details are in the privacy policy list.

item.title: Convert an HWP file to PDF on Android – SugarMount
item.description:
Help · Android

Convert an HWP file to PDF on Android

Open the HWP or HWPX file in HWP Viewer SugarDoc, tap ⋮ (More options) and then Save as PDF, and pick a folder. The PDF is made on your phone without uploading the document. Long documents are cut to the first 15 pages.

This guide is based on HWP Viewer SugarDoc 1.2.0, an Android app made by SugarMount. The Save as PDF menu item arrived in 1.2.0; on older versions use the print screen instead (see below). The screenshots show the app in Korean.

Without an app, and the catch

HWP and HWPX are Korean word-processor formats, and Android phones usually have no app that opens them. If the phone cannot open the file, it cannot print it to PDF either, so the app-free options are all off the phone:

  • Ask the sender for a PDF. They export it from the program that made it, so the layout matches best. You have to wait for a reply.
  • Save as PDF in a desktop HWP program. Good for long documents where layout matters. Needs a computer with the program.
  • Upload to a web converter. Nothing to install, but the file goes to that site's server. Avoid it for letters or forms with names, phone numbers or addresses.

Save as PDF in HWP Viewer SugarDoc

  1. Open the document — tap the HWP or HWPX file in KakaoTalk, email or your file manager and choose HWP Viewer from Open with or Share, or pick it with Find in my files inside the app.
  2. ⋮ → Save as PDF — tap ⋮ at the top right of the document and choose Save as PDF.
  3. Check the page notice — if the document is longer than the limit, the app tells you how many pages will be saved first. Tap Save to go on or Cancel to stop without making a file.
  4. Pick where to save — Android's save screen opens with the document's name plus .pdf filled in. Choose a folder and tap Save.
  5. Done — the message "Saved as a PDF." appears. The HWP or HWPX file you received is not changed.

Checked on a Galaxy S21 (Android 15) with the SugarDoc 1.2.0 release build on October 18, 2026: a 47-page HWP document showed the notice and produced a 15-page PDF, and a 3-page HWPX document was saved with all 3 pages.

Save through the print screen

Tap Print in the ⋮ menu to open Android's print screen (on versions before 1.2.0 the item is called Print or save as PDF). Under Select printer, choose the save-as-PDF option (its name varies by phone) to keep the result as a PDF file. Use this if Save as PDF fails; the same page limit applies.

"In Android 4.4 (API level 19) and higher, the framework provides services for printing images and documents directly from Android applications."

Source: Android Developers, Printing content

Which way to use

MethodPhone onlyUploadLengthUse it when
SugarDoc Save as PDFYesNoneFirst 15 pages (6 on low-memory phones)You need a short notice or letter as a PDF right now
SugarDoc Print → PDFYesNoneSame as aboveSave as PDF failed, or you are on a version before 1.2.0 (there the item is ‘Print or save as PDF’)
Ask the senderYes (you wait)NoneNo limitThe layout must match, or it is longer than 15 pages
Desktop HWP programNoNoneDepends on the programYou need to edit a long document first
Web converterYesTo their serverVaries by siteThe document has no personal information

Verdict: for a document of 15 pages or fewer that you need as a PDF now, Save as PDF in the app is the quickest. For longer documents or forms where layout matters, get a PDF from the sender or make it on a computer.

Limits and what to do when it fails

  • Only the first pages are saved. Usually the first 15, or the first 6 on phones with little memory. You cannot choose a page range.
  • Distribution-only documents cannot be saved. When printing and copying are locked, Save as PDF and Print do not appear in the menu.
  • PDF files have no Save as PDF. They are already PDFs, so only Print is offered, and a password-protected PDF cannot be printed.
  • Layout may differ slightly. If the original fonts are not on your phone, similar fonts are used, so line breaks and spacing can shift. Open the saved PDF and check it before you submit it anywhere.
  • If it will not open, it will not save. Documents locked by a company DRM program cannot be opened. If the file does not open at all, start with what to check when an HWPX file will not open.
  • No PDF-to-HWP. SugarDoc is a viewer only.

About the HWP format

HWP is the native format of the Hancom word processor widely used in Korea. Its specification is public, which is why other apps can read it. Hancom says (in Korean) that it published the HWP binary format and the HWPML markup language on June 29, 2010: "한컴은 2010년 6월 29일에 자사의 바이너리 포맷인 HWP와 마크업 언어인 HWPML을 공개하였습니다."

Source: Hancom download center, HWP and OWPML formats. For how .hwp and .hwpx differ, see HWP vs HWPX.

FAQ

Does saving as PDF cost anything?

No. Save as PDF and Print need no payment, and the app has no ads.

Is my document uploaded anywhere?

No. SugarDoc does not send documents to a server; the PDF is made on your phone. See the HWP Viewer SugarDoc privacy policy.

Where is the saved PDF?

In the folder you picked on the save screen. The folder shown first can differ by phone, so check its name before you tap Save. Afterwards you can find the PDF in your phone's Files app.

Can I convert a document longer than 15 pages in full?

Not in SugarDoc. Only the first 15 pages (6 on low-memory phones) are saved. For the whole document, ask the sender for a PDF or make it on a computer.

If I cancel on the save screen, is an empty file left behind?

No. Cancelling on the save screen creates no file.

  • When an HWPX file will not open on your phone
  • HWP and HWPX: what is the difference

item.title: HWP vs HWPX: what differs and how to open both – SugarMount
item.description:
Help · Android

HWP vs HWPX: what differs and how to open both

HWP and HWPX are both Korean Hangul documents, but they are built differently, so renaming the file does not convert it. On an Android phone, open both with one viewer; converting HWPX to HWP needs the Hangul word processor on a PC.

This article uses SugarMount's Android app HWP Viewer SugarDoc (SugarDoc for short; shown as "HWP Viewer" on your phone). It cannot convert HWPX to HWP or HWP to HWPX. Editing (Pro) covers body and table cell text in HWP documents only; HWPX documents cannot be edited yet.

How HWP and HWPX differ

.hwp is the long-standing format of Hancom's Hangul word processor, common in Korean schools, offices and government. It is a binary compound file, so its contents are not human-readable. .hwpx is the newer open format (OWPML): the document is written as XML files packed into one ZIP archive.

Hancom states which versions support each format:

"HWP의 개방형 문서 형식인 OWPML은 HWP 2018 버전부터 ".owpml" 확장자로 지원하고 있으며, 하위 버전은 HWP 2010 버전부터 ".hwpx" 확장자로 지원하고 있습니다."

In English: OWPML, HWP's open document format, is supported with the ".owpml" extension from HWP 2018, and with the ".hwpx" extension from HWP 2010. The same page describes the .hwp 5.x format as the one used from HWP 2002 through HWP 2018. Source: Hancom Download Center, HWP/OWPML format (Korean, checked October 18, 2026).

So the same letter can arrive in either format. An app that reads only one of them cannot open the other, and changing the extension leaves the inside unchanged.

Side by side

Item.hwp.hwpx
Inside the fileBinary compound fileXML files in a ZIP (OWPML)
Hangul word processor support (per Hancom)5.x format from HWP 2002From HWP 2010
Rename the extensionDoes not work. The inside stays the same
Open in SugarDocYes, including old HWP 3.0Yes
Password-protectedOpens with the password. Password-protected HWP 3.0 files cannot be openedOpens with the password
Convert between them in SugarDocNo

Verdict: if you only need to read the document, the difference does not matter; one app that opens both is enough. The format only matters when you must send the file on to someone using a Hangul version older than HWP 2010. Then re-save it as .hwp on a PC, or send a PDF.

Without an app, and the limits

  • Renaming the file: does not work. A .hwpx renamed to .hwp is still a ZIP-based HWPX inside, so programs that cannot read HWPX still fail.
  • Re-saving in the Hangul word processor on a PC: the usual way to get .hwp. Open the file in a version that supports .hwpx, then save a copy and choose the .hwp file type. Menu names vary by version, and you need a PC with the program.
  • Asking the sender for another format: the most reliable. The author can re-save as .hwp or PDF with the fewest layout changes, but you have to wait for a reply.
  • Your phone's built-in apps: usually open neither. Android phones generally have a PDF viewer but no app for .hwp or .hwpx.

Open either format with SugarDoc

  1. Tap the file — In KakaoTalk, email or your file manager, tap the .hwp or .hwpx file and pick HWP Viewer from "Open with" or "Share". For a file already saved on the phone, use Find in my files in the app.
  2. Don't choose a format — There is nothing to pick. The app tells HWP, HWPX and PDF apart by reading the file's contents, not by the extension at the end of its name.
  3. Find it again later — Every document you open is listed with its format (HWP, HWPX or PDF). When the list grows, search by file name.
  4. Enter the password if asked — A password-protected HWP or HWPX file opens once you type its password. The password is not saved.

Screenshots are real app screens captured for SugarDoc's store listing. Menu names can differ slightly by app version and phone model.

What it cannot do

  • No format conversion. SugarDoc cannot turn HWPX into HWP or the other way round, and it cannot create documents. Editing (Pro) covers body and table cell text in HWP documents only.
  • You can keep a PDF. If the recipient has no Hangul word processor, or an old one, a PDF may be the easiest thing to send. See convert an HWP file to PDF on Android for the steps and page limits.
  • Layout may differ slightly. When the original font is not on your phone, a similar font is used, so line breaks and spacing can shift. Old HWP 3.0 files may differ more.
  • Some files will not open. DRM-protected documents, password-protected HWP 3.0 files and files over 1 GB cannot be opened. Distribution-only documents may not open, or show only a preview.
  • Other office formats are not supported. Excel, Word and PowerPoint files do not open.

If a file does not open at all, the cause is usually your phone's app settings rather than the format. Start with when an HWPX file won't open on your phone.

FAQ

If I rename .hwpx to .hwp, will it open?

No. Only the name changes; the file is still HWPX inside, so programs that cannot read HWPX still fail. To get a real .hwp, re-save it as .hwp in a Hangul word processor that supports .hwpx.

Can SugarDoc convert HWPX to HWP?

No. SugarDoc has no format conversion. It opens both formats, and you can keep the document as a PDF.

Which format should I ask for?

For reading, either is fine; an app that opens both shows them the same way. If you must forward the file to someone using a Hangul version older than HWP 2010, .hwp or PDF is safer.

Do very old HWP 3.0 files open?

Yes, SugarDoc opens them, though they may look more different from the original. Password-protected HWP 3.0 files cannot be opened.

Are my documents uploaded anywhere?

No. SugarDoc opens documents on your phone without uploading them, and it never changes the original file. See the privacy policy for details.

item.title: How to open an HWPX or HWP file on Android – SugarMount
item.description:
Help · Android

How to open an HWPX or HWP file on Android

An HWPX or HWP file usually will not open on Android because the phone has no app for Korean word-processor documents. Install an HWP viewer, then choose it from Open with in KakaoTalk, email or your file manager.

This guide uses HWP Viewer SugarDoc, an Android app made by SugarMount; other HWP viewers work much the same way. Menu names vary a little by app version and phone. The screenshots are cropped from the app's Google Play screenshots of version 1.0.0.

Why the file will not open

  • No app can read it. Android phones usually come with something that opens PDFs, but nothing for .hwp or .hwpx. Tapping the file ends with a message that no app can open it.
  • The file arrives as an unknown type. Some apps hand over .hwpx as a generic file instead of a document, so a viewer you have installed may still be missing from the list of apps.
  • Another app is the default. If you once tapped Always for a different app, that app opens straight away without asking. If it cannot read HWPX you see a blank screen or an error.

HWPX is the newer of the two formats. Hancom, the maker of the Hangul word processor, says (in Korean) that its open format OWPML has been supported with the .hwpx extension since Hangul 2010:

  • Ask the sender for a PDF. Every Android phone can show a PDF, and the layout matches the original best. You have to wait for a reply.
  • Open it on a computer with the Hangul word processor or another program that reads HWP. Not much help when you need the file on the go.
  • Upload it to a web viewer or converter. Nothing to install, but the document goes to that site's server. Avoid it for school letters, forms or anything with names, phone numbers or addresses.

  1. Install an HWP viewer — get an app that opens HWP and HWPX from Google Play. HWP Viewer SugarDoc shows no permission prompts after installing and needs no sign-up.

When the viewer is missing from the list

Go to Android Settings > Apps > that app > Open by default (or a similar name on your phone) and clear its defaults, then tap the file again; the list of apps comes back. Android's developer guide describes how a default gets set:

"When there is more than one app that responds to your implicit intent, the user can select which app to use and make that app the default choice for the action."

Source: Android Developers, Intents and intent filters (checked October 18, 2026).

If it still will not open

Resize an ID photo for Korean application uploads

Korean upload forms often cap ID photos at a file size such as 500 KB. Compress Image saves your photo as a JPEG under the limit you set. It does not crop to a ratio, so crop first if pixel sizes are fixed.

This guide uses Compress Image 1.0.6, an Android app made by SugarMount. Rules differ by site, so we don't invent numbers here; the only example is the Korean passport photo, which has an official guide.

Check the site's rules first

Photo fields on Korean application, job and government sites usually set three separate conditions. Meeting one of them is not always enough.

  • File size: written as "500KB 이하" (500 KB or less). This is what the app fits.
  • Pixel size: for example 413 × 531 pixels. A fixed ratio means the photo must be cropped to it.
  • File type: usually JPG (JPEG). The app always saves JPEG.

The rules are in the notice or next to the upload button. For any site not covered here, follow that notice.

Without an app, and the limits

  • Ask the photo studio for a file: studios can often hand over a digital file sized for submission. This is the surest route, but you need to go back if the photo is already taken.
  • Your gallery app's editor: most Android gallery apps can crop, which handles the ratio. Menu names and resize options vary by phone and version, so we don't list them. After saving, check the real file size and pixels in the photo's details.
  • For a passport photo, the government resize tool: the Ministry of Foreign Affairs passport site has an online passport photo resize tool (Korean only). You upload a photo, zoom and move it until the face fits a red dotted guide, then save. It accepts JPG or PNG under 1 MB, and the page says the result is not for ID, half-size or visa photos.

Shrink it with Compress Image

  1. Select photos: tap Select photos on the first screen and pick the ID photo. The app uses the Android photo picker, so it asks for no storage permission.
  2. Method: Fit to size: on the Options screen, choose Fit to size under Method.
  3. Pick the limit: under Size limit per photo, pick 100 KB, 200 KB, 500 KB or 1 MB, equal to or below the site's limit. If none matches, tap Custom and enter 20 to 20000 KB.
  4. Set the long edge if pixels are fixed: on the same screen, open Long edge, tap the custom option and enter 320 to 8000 px. The aspect ratio stays the same, so if you already cropped to the required ratio, the short edge follows. A photo cropped to 3.5 : 4.5 with a long edge of 531 comes out at 413 × 531 pixels.
  5. Check the result: tap Create results. Each photo shows its size before → after and its width × height in pixels. These are the real sizes of the files that will be saved.
  6. Save or share: Save all writes new files to Pictures/SugarCompress, and Share sends them straight to another app. Your original photos are not changed.

Screens are real app captures taken on an Android emulator in September 2026 for the Play listing, with sample pictures. Menu labels match the app's 1.0.6 source.

Korean passport photo upload rules

The passport site lists the files it accepts for online renewal (quoted in Korean, our translation below):

"파일 크기 500KB 이하, 파일 형식 JPG/JPEG"
"가로 413 픽셀(pixel), 세로 531 픽셀 사이즈 권장(가로 395~431 픽셀, 세로 507~550 픽셀 이내만 업로드 가능)"

File size 500 KB or less, JPG/JPEG. Recommended 413 pixels wide by 531 high; only 395–431 wide and 507–550 high can be uploaded. Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs passport site, photo files for online applications, checked October 18, 2026. Rules can change, so check again before you submit.

The app can meet the size, the JPEG type and the long edge. It does not judge head size, the white background or whether the photo was taken in the last six months. The same page also advises against phone photos:

"휴대폰 등 모바일 기기로 촬영된 사진, 사진 편집 프로그램 등으로 과도한 보정을 한 사진은 여권 발급 시 사진이 실물과 다르게 표현될 수 있으므로 권장하지 않음"

Photos taken on phones or heavily retouched are not recommended, because they may look different from the person in the issued passport.

You can test the result with the site's online passport photo check. The site says this check is for reference and the real review may differ.

MethodSet a size limitCrop to a ratioSet pixelsWhere it works
Compress Image appYes (20 KB–20 MB)NoLong edge only (320–8000 px)Any site with a size limit
Gallery app editorVaries by phoneUsually (crop)Varies by phoneAnywhere on the phone
Passport photo resize toolNot statedYes (face to guide)Set by the toolPassport online application only
Studio fileIf you askYesIf you askWhen taking a new photo

Verdict: if the site only sets a file size, the app alone is enough. If it also fixes the ratio and pixels, as for passports, crop first (for passports, use the official tool), then use the app last for the size and long edge.

When it doesn't work, and limits

  • No cropping to a ratio. The aspect ratio stays as it is. Crop in your gallery app or the passport tool first.
  • No enlarging. If the original is smaller than required, a larger long edge changes nothing. Get the original file or a studio file instead.
  • Pixels may shrink too. If lower quality still misses the limit, the app reduces the long edge and tries again, never below 320 px. Always check the pixel size on the result screen.

The site counts 1 KB as 1024 bytes. Is that a problem?

No. The app counts 1 KB as 1000 bytes, so a file fitted to 500 KB is at most 500,000 bytes. That is below 500 KB counted in 1024-byte units (512,000 bytes), so it passes either way.

Does it change or delete my original photo?

No. Results are saved as new files in Pictures/SugarCompress, and the original stays as it was.

No. Photos are processed on your phone and never uploaded. See the Compress Image privacy policy for details.

Yes, if your phone can decode HEIC. The result is saved as JPEG. To change only the format, see Convert HEIC to JPG on a Samsung Galaxy phone.

It is free with ads and handles 20 photos at a time. Pro, a one-time purchase, removes ads and handles 100 at a time. Each photo can be up to 50 MB and 50 megapixels.

Compress a photo to under 100 KB on Android

Your phone's gallery can make a photo smaller, but it can't promise a file size. When a form says "under 100 KB", use an app that lets you type the limit in KB and checks the real file size.

This guide uses Compress Image (SugarCompress) 1.0.6, an Android app made by SugarMount. Gallery menu names vary by phone model and software version.

Without an app: Resize in the Galaxy Gallery

The built-in Gallery app on Galaxy phones can shrink a photo's dimensions. Samsung's support guide lists these steps:

  2. Tap More options (the three dots) and choose Resize.
  3. Pick a percentage, tap Done, then Save. To keep the original, choose Save copy from More options before saving.

"Resizing the photo to be larger than its original size is not an option."

Source: Samsung UK, How to resize a photo in the Gallery app on your Galaxy phone. The same page notes: "The resize feature may not be supported depending on the model version."

Limits of this method

  • You choose a percentage, not a file size. You have to save, check the file size, and resize again if it is still too big.
  • A plain save can replace the original. Samsung's guide says that on Android 11 saving overwrites the original unless you pick Save copy.
  • One photo at a time. The guide covers editing a single photo.

Some image compression websites let you set a size in KB, but your photo is uploaded to their server. For ID photos or document scans, that may matter to you.

Fit a photo under 100 KB with Compress Image

  1. Tap 100 KB — Under Quick start on the home screen, tap 100 KB. This sets the limit to 100 KB and opens the photo picker. You can also tap Select photos and set the limit on the next screen.
  2. Pick photos — Choose photos in the Android photo picker. The free version handles up to 20 at a time. Check the list and tap Next.
  3. Check the limit and create — On the Options screen, make sure the method is Fit to size and the size limit per photo is 100 KB. For another number, use Custom and enter 20 to 20000 KB. Tap Create results.

A JPEG result is never larger than the original. If the photo is already small enough, the app keeps it at original quality without recompressing and removes only location and camera info.

Help · Android

Convert HEIC to JPG on a Samsung Galaxy phone

To turn HEIC photos you already took into JPG, use a converter app that saves new JPG files. Convert Image does several at once on your phone, without uploading, and leaves the originals untouched.

This article is based on Convert Image JPG PNG WEBP 1.0.3, an Android app made by SugarMount. If you want future photos saved as JPG from the start, read "Without an app" first.

HEIC vs JPG

HEIC is a file in the HEIF photo format, compressed with HEVC (H.265). JPG is far older, and almost every website, program and printer accepts it. That is why a HEIC photo that looks fine on your phone can be rejected by an upload form or fail to open on a PC.

Whether Android itself can read HEIC depends on the device. The supported formats table in the Android developer documentation says this about HEIF decoding:

"Android 9.0+ … Device optional. Check ImageDecoder.isMimeTypeSupported("image/heif") for 8-bit support. 10-bit decoding requires optional HEVC Main10 profile."

Source: Android Developers, Supported media formats

Without an app, and the limits

  • Turn off HEIF (high efficiency) saving in the camera — some phones have a camera setting for it. With it off, new photos are saved as JPG. The menu name and place vary by model and version. Photos you already took stay HEIC.
  • Conversion when sharing from the gallery — depending on the model, the gallery may have a setting that sends photos as JPG when you share them. It only applies to what you share, and may not leave a JPG file on the phone.
  • Convert on a PC — the PC program has to read HEIC, and you need to move the photos first.
  • Upload to a converter website — no install, but the photos go to that site's server. Avoid it for photos of faces, IDs or documents.

Convert HEIC to JPG with Convert Image

Use Pick from files to keep the original file names: the photo picker does not share names, so photos picked there are saved as "SugarConvert + time". The JPG for forms quick start (quality 90, transparent areas white) starts with JPG settings ready.
  2. Check the selection — the Selected photos screen shows the count and total size. If HEIC photos are included, a notice says they convert only where the device can decode them. Tap Next.
  3. Choose JPEG — under Output format on Convert options, choose JPEG and set the quality. The default is 90; lower values give smaller files. Then tap Create results.
  4. Check and save — the Results screen shows the real size and resolution before and after. Tap Save all. The JPG files are saved as new files in Pictures/SugarConvert; the original HEIC files are not changed.
  5. If some photos fail — a HEIC the device cannot decode is marked as failed on its own, and the rest continue. Retry failed only runs just those again. If they keep failing on the same phone, see "When it fails, and the limits".

  • HEIC the device cannot decode is not converted. The app reads photos with the phone's own decoder. Without one, or for HEIC the device does not support (such as 10-bit), that photo fails. Use a PC instead.

item.title: PNG to JPG on Android with a white background – SugarMount
item.description:
PNG to JPG on Android with a white background

JPG cannot store transparency, so converting a PNG to JPG fills its transparent areas with one solid colour. On Android, choose that colour in a converter app, set it to white, and save the result.

This guide uses SugarMount's Android app Convert Image JPG PNG WEBP (SugarConvert). Other converters work on the same principle: transparent areas always become a colour.

Without an app, and the catch

There are two common ways to convert without installing anything on the phone.

  • A web converter — upload the PNG in a browser and download a JPG. Nothing to install, but the image goes to that site's server. Not a good fit for IDs or documents, and the fill colour for transparent areas and the number of files per run vary by site.
  • An image editor on a computer — move the file to a PC and save it as JPEG. No upload, but you have to move files back and forth, and the colour transparent areas turn into depends on the program.

Either way, the JPG keeps no transparency. Check that the formerly transparent area is the colour you want.

Convert with the app

  1. Check the preset — on the home screen, make sure JPG for forms is selected: quality 90, transparent areas white. It is the default the first time you open the app.
  2. Pick the PNG files — tap Select photos or Pick from files. Use Pick from files to keep the original file names; the system photo picker does not share names, so those files are saved as SugarConvert plus the time. If a PNG has transparent areas, the Selected photos screen tells you they will be filled with the background colour. Tap Next.
  3. Choose the background colour — on Convert options, check that the output format is JPEG and pick White, Black or Gray under Transparent areas. Set quality between 40 and 100 (default 90) and check the preview.
  4. Create and save — tap Create results, compare the original and the result side by side, then tap Save all. Items whose transparency was filled are marked "transparent areas filled with white". Results are saved as new files in Pictures/SugarConvert; the original PNG stays as it was.

Screens are cropped from the store captures in the app's repository. Wording and layout may differ slightly between app versions.

Which method to use

MethodUploadColour for transparent areasSeveral files at onceVerdict
Web converterYes, to the site's serverVaries by siteVaries by siteFine for one or two non-sensitive images
Image editor on a PCNoVaries by programUsually one at a timeGood if the file is already on the PC
Convert Image appNo, converted on the deviceWhite, Black or Gray20 free, 100 with ProEasiest for several PNGs already on the phone

Why transparency turns into a colour

PNG can store how transparent each pixel is. The W3C PNG specification says:

“Indexed-color, greyscale, and truecolor images are supported, plus an optional alpha channel.”

Source: W3C, Portable Network Graphics (PNG) Specification (Third Edition). The alpha channel is the transparency data.

JPEG has no such data. The Android developer documentation notes it when describing how images are compressed and saved:

“JPEG only supports opaque pixels”

Source: Android Developers, Bitmap.compress().

So a PNG-to-JPG conversion has to decide what colour goes where the image was transparent. The app paints the chosen colour first and draws the image on top, so soft, semi-transparent edges blend into that colour. A PNG with no transparent areas converts the same whatever colour you pick.

What it can't do

  • A JPG cannot keep transparency. If you need it, save as PNG or WebP and choose Keep for transparent areas.
  • The background can only be white, black or gray. There is no custom colour.
  • Converting a JPG back to PNG does not restore lost detail or transparency, and the file may get larger.
  • Animated images are not converted; that item fails and the rest continue. Each image can be up to 50 MB and 50 MP.
  • No cropping or background removal. The only resize is shrinking the long edge.
  • Location and camera data (EXIF) are not copied to the result.

FAQ

Does converting PNG to JPG lower the quality?

JPEG is lossy, so some detail is lost depending on the quality value. The default of 90 looks the same as the original for most photos; lower values give smaller files. The Results screen shows the real file sizes.

Can I fill transparency with black instead of white?

Yes. Pick Black or Gray under Transparent areas on the Convert options screen. Other colours are not available.

Will the JPG be smaller?

Photos with many colours usually get smaller, but simple graphics can get larger. If a result is larger than the original, the Results screen says so.

Where are the converted files saved?

As new files in the phone's Pictures/SugarConvert folder. The original PNG is not changed or deleted.

Are my images uploaded?

No. Conversion happens on the device and nothing is uploaded. See the Convert Image privacy policy for details.

Help · Android

Unmirror a selfie on a Samsung Galaxy phone

To fix a selfie you already took, flip it left to right and save it as a new photo. Google Photos does one picture at a time; the Flip & Rotate Image app's "Selfie as others see it" preset fixes a whole batch at once.

This article is based on Flip & Rotate Image 1.0.3, an Android app made by SugarMount. The screens below are store captures of version 1.0.0 with demo photos; the menus shown are the same in 1.0.3.

Why selfies look flipped

While you take a selfie, the front camera shows you a mirror image, so you see the face you know from the mirror. Other people see the opposite. The Android developer documentation describes the front-camera preview like this:

"Note that preview display of front-facing cameras is flipped horizontally before the rotation, that is, the image is reflected along the central vertical axis of the camera sensor. So the users can see themselves as looking into a mirror."

Source: Android Developers, Camera.setDisplayOrientation. This is the older camera API, but the mirrored preview works the same way.

Whether the saved photo keeps that mirror view or is stored the way others see you depends on the phone and its camera settings. Galaxy camera settings include a related option, but its name and location vary by model and software version, so we don't name it here. It applies to photos you take from then on; photos you already took stay as they are. Fix those with one of the methods below.

Without a new app, and the limits

If your phone has Google Photos, you can mirror one photo at a time in its editor. The Google Photos Help Center gives these steps:

  1. Open the photo in Google Photos and tap Edit at the bottom.
  2. Tap Crop, then Mirror.
  3. Tap the checkmark (Done), then choose Save or Save as copy.

"Save: Saves your changes to the original photo." "Save as copy: Makes a new photo with your edits without changes to the original."

Source: Google Photos Help, Edit your photos (Android)

Limits: one photo at a time. "Save" changes the original, so pick "Save as copy" if you want to keep it. Menu names can change between Google Photos versions. The Galaxy Gallery editor also differs by version, so we don't cover it here.

Fix many selfies at once with Flip & Rotate Image

  1. Tap "Selfie as others see it" — Under Quick start on the home screen, tap Selfie as others see it. It sets a left-right flip and opens the photo picker right away.
  2. Pick your selfies — Choose them in the Android photo picker: up to 20 at a time for free, 100 with Pro. Check the list and tap Next.
  3. Check the preview — The Transform screen lists "1 · Flip left ↔ right" under Applied in order. Compare the original with the preview and leave the output format on "Keep original". Tap Create results.
  4. Save and share — On the Results screen, compare the original and the result again, then tap Save all. The results go into the Pictures/SugarFlip folder as new files and the originals stay untouched. You can also tap Share.

The app applies the orientation your phone recorded in the photo (EXIF) first, so the flip follows the way the photo looks in your gallery. The same steps also turn an already unmirrored selfie back into the mirror view.

Methods compared

MethodPhotos already takenMany photosOriginalBest for
Change the camera settingNot changed——Choosing how future selfies are saved
Google Photos MirrorYesOne at a time"Save" changes it; "Save as copy" makes a new photoFixing one or two photos
Flip & Rotate Image, "Selfie as others see it"Yes20 free, 100 with ProAlways saved as a new file; original untouchedFixing a batch the same way at once

Verdict: for one or two photos, Google Photos' Mirror with "Save as copy" is quickest. For a batch of selfies from a trip or a party, Flip & Rotate Image is easier. To change future selfies, check your camera settings separately.

When it doesn't work, and limits

  • It doesn't change your camera settings. The app fixes photos you already took; new selfies are still saved the way your camera is set.
  • Photos only. Selfie videos and animated images (such as animated WebP) can't be flipped.
  • You can't send photos to it with Share from your gallery. Pick them inside the app with "Select photos" or a preset.
  • Photo details (EXIF) are not kept in the result. If you need the date or location, keep the original.
  • JPEGs are saved again at quality 95. The resolution stays the same, but the file isn't identical to the original and its size can change a little.
  • Each photo can be up to 50 MB and 50 megapixels.
  • Two left-right flips produce no result. They cancel out, and the app tells you so. Tap "Reset" under Applied in order and pick again.

FAQ

The text in my selfie is backwards. Will flipping fix it?

Yes. Backwards text means the photo was saved as a mirror image; flipping it left to right makes the text readable.

Will my original selfie be changed or deleted?

Flip & Rotate Image leaves the original alone and writes a new file to Pictures/SugarFlip. In Google Photos, "Save" changes the original, so choose "Save as copy".

Are my photos uploaded anywhere?

No. Flip & Rotate Image processes photos on your phone and doesn't upload them. See the Flip & Rotate Image privacy policy for details.

Does flipping lower the quality?

The resolution stays the same. JPEGs are saved again at quality 95, so the file isn't byte-for-byte identical. The Results screen shows the size before and after.

Can future selfies be saved the way others see me?

That is set in your phone's camera app. Flip & Rotate Image doesn't change camera settings.

Korean Christmas greeting card messages

A Korean Christmas greeting only needs one or two sentences that fit the person. You can send the words on their own, or use SugarCard to put them on a card and send it as an image or a snowfall video.

This guide is based on SugarCard 1.0.002, an Android app made by SugarMount. The app is in Korean. The example messages below were written for this page; the app has no built-in messages, so you type your own.

Example messages by recipient

Each line is Korean first, then what it means. Adding a name or one thing from this year makes it feel less formal. If the message goes on a card, two short lines read best.

Parents and family

  • 올 한 해도 늘 먼저 챙겨 주셔서 고마워요. 따뜻한 성탄절 보내세요.
  • Thank you for always looking after us this year. Have a warm Christmas.
  • 가족 모두 건강하게 한 해를 마무리할 수 있어서 감사한 성탄이에요.

  5. Pick the app — Your phone's share screen opens. Choose KakaoTalk, Messages or another app.

That last screen is Android's own share screen. The Android developer documentation describes it like this:

"The Android Sharesheet is primarily designed for sending content outside your app or directly to another user."

So the list of apps you can send to depends on what is installed on your phone. Source: Android Developers, Send data to other apps

item.description:
Help · Android

Spell-check long Korean text on Android

The common Korean web spell checkers take 300 or 1,000 characters at a time. On Android, SugarSpeller checks up to 3,000 free, or 7,000 with a subscription, in one pass.

This guide is based on the source of SugarSpeller 1.6.031, an Android app by SugarMount (its home-screen name is Hangul Checker). It is not unlimited: text over 7,000 characters still has to be split.

Without an app, and the limits

Most people paste text into a portal's web spell checker. When we checked on October 18, 2026, the checker on Naver's search results showed a 0/300 counter, and Daum's spell checker page showed 0/1000. Spaces count as characters.

  • Long text must be split. A 2,000-character cover letter takes 7 rounds in a 300-character checker and 2 in a 1,000-character one. Cutting mid-paragraph can change how spacing is judged.
  • You stitch the results back together. Each corrected piece has to be copied back in order by hand.
  • Fine on a PC, tedious on a phone. Selecting and splitting long text on a small screen is the slow part.

If you check spacing by hand, the basic rule is in the official Korean spelling standard, Chapter 1, Article 2, from the National Institute of Korean Language:

"문장의 각 단어는 띄어 씀을 원칙으로 한다."

"As a rule, each word in a sentence is written with a space." Source: National Institute of Korean Language, Korean Orthography, Chapter 1, Article 2

Check long text with SugarSpeller

  1. Add your text — Paste it into the input box at the bottom, or pick Hangul Checker from another app's Share menu. Shared text goes into the input box first; it is not checked until you send it.
  2. Watch the count — While you type, the app shows the count against your limit, like "1234/3000". Anything past the limit does not go into the box, so if the count equals the limit, your text was cut. Check the rest separately.
  3. Send — Tap the send button. The app splits the text into pieces of about 300 characters, at a space, period or line break, checks them, and shows the result as one text again.
  4. Review corrections — Tap an underlined part to see the original and the correction side by side. Tap Why is it wrong? for a short AI explanation.
  5. Copy or share — Use the copy and share buttons under the result to move the corrected text where you need it.

Screens: Galaxy S21 (real device), SugarSpeller 1.6.025 with the Korean interface, captured October 1, 2026, status bar cropped. The character limits and piece size were checked in the 1.6.031 source. The layout may differ slightly between versions.

Characters per check, compared

MethodPer checkA 2,000-character textCostUse it when
Web checker (search results)3007 roundsFreeYou need a sentence or two checked fast
Web checker (dictionary page)1,0002 roundsFreeYou're on a PC with medium-length text
SugarSpeller Free3,000One passFree (with ads)You want a whole essay answer checked on your phone
SugarSpeller Basic4,000One passSubscription (banner ads)Your texts often run a little over 3,000
SugarSpeller Premium7,000One passSubscription (no ads)You check several answers together

Verdict: for text up to 3,000 characters on a phone, the free app is enough. For longer text, split it by question for free, or subscribe if you do this often. For one or two sentences, a web checker is fine and needs no install.

Limits and when it fails

  • It is not unlimited. Free 3,000, Basic 4,000, Premium 7,000 characters. Spaces and line breaks count.
  • It needs the internet. The app does not judge spelling itself. It sends the text to the Naver or Daum (Kakao) spell checker. Which one is used is set by the app's configuration server; if one fails, the app retries once with the other.
  • Slow checks fail. If not every piece comes back within 30 seconds, the app stops and asks you to try again.
  • Shared text loses line breaks. Text received through Share has runs of spaces and line breaks merged into single spaces. If paragraphs matter, paste into the box instead.
  • The text-selection menu is for short text. Select text in another app and pick Spell check: up to 300 characters are checked in a small sheet; longer text is passed to the main screen.
  • It fixes only what the checker catches. It does not judge whether a sentence reads well or is correct. Read it aloud once before you submit.

Where your text goes

Text you check is sent to the Naver or Daum (Kakao) spell checker. Only when you tap Why is it wrong?, the original words, the corrected words and the error type go through SugarMount's server (Google Firebase) to Google Vertex AI. Surrounding sentences are not sent. Keep this in mind for text with personal details, such as a cover letter. See the SugarSpeller privacy policy for details.

The text-selection menu is a standard Android feature that hands selected text to an app. The Android developer reference describes it as:

"Activity Action: Process a piece of text."

Source: Android Developers, Intent.ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT

FAQ

Is there a Korean spell checker with no character limit?

SugarSpeller has limits too: 3,000 characters free, 4,000 with Basic and 7,000 with Premium. Split longer text by paragraph or question.

Do spaces count?

Yes. The app's count and limit include spaces and line breaks, so it can differ from a "without spaces" count on an application form.

What happens if I paste more than 3,000 characters?

The part past the limit does not go into the box. If the count reads "3000/3000", your text was cut; paste the rest and check it separately.

Is my checked text saved?

Originals and corrections are kept in the check history on your phone. Turn off the "Save check history" setting if you don't want new checks saved.

Do I need an account?

No sign-up is needed. Checking does need an internet connection.

item.title: Four Android apps in 20 days with an AI agent – SugarMount
item.description:
AX notes · Measured case

How we shipped four Android apps in 20 days with an AI coding agent

Working with an AI coding agent (Claude Code), a solo developer published four Android apps on Google Play in the 20 days from the first commit on September 20, 2026 to October 10.

In that period 52 of 59 commits (88%) are marked as co-authored with the agent. The speed did not come only from the AI writing code fast. Each app was stamped out from the same template, one at a time, and pre-release checks and Play Console work were turned into scripts.

The numbers come from the git history, CHANGELOG and on-device QA reports of SugarMount's app repository (sugar-utils), as of October 18, 2026.

What happened in those 20 days?

DateWhat was done
09-20Repository started. The skeleton of the first app, Compress Image, and the shared file, image, ads and analytics modules written in parallel by several agents in separate git worktrees
09-21First signed AAB (1.0.0). A script that uploads builds and store listings through the Play Developer API
09-23An R8 problem that crashed the release build right after launch found on a real device (Galaxy S23) and fixed
09-24The second app, Flip & Rotate Image, and the third, Convert Image, generated from the scaffolding script and uploaded to the internal test track
09-25On-device QA of all three apps on a Galaxy S21 by four agents in turn (one per app, then one independent cross-check)
10-03First app's store page live
10-04Defects from end-to-end tests on a Galaxy S20 and S21 fixed; all three apps released to production
10-10Fourth app, HWP Viewer SugarDoc, store page live

41 of the 59 commits (69%) were made between 9 p.m. and 2 a.m. This was not full-time work but a few hours each evening.

How was the work split between the person and the AI?

AI agent

  • Kotlin code and unit tests
  • Build, release and QA scripts
  • Store listing drafts, screenshot capture and framing
  • Emulator and device tests, with written reports

Person

  • Decisions such as ad placement, prices and tone of copy (recorded with a date in the instruction file)
  • Work that only the Play Console can do
  • Connecting real devices and the final check
  • The decision to release to production

The co-author mark means the commit was made together with the agent. It is not a measure of who wrote how many lines.

Four rules that made it fast

  1. One app at a time, shared code in modules — File saving, image processing, job state, ads, billing and analytics live in core/ modules, not in an app. From the second app on, only the screens and the app's own feature are new.
  2. Stamp out the next app with a script — new_app.sh copies the first app, changes its name, colour and icon, and blanks every per-app identifier to PLACEHOLDER. Its first real run (09-23) exposed four bugs, which were fixed; the next day the third app was generated without a single change.
  3. Let a gate stop easy mistakes — A release build is not produced while an ad test ID remains or an identifier is empty. Rules do not stop at the instruction file; tests enforce them (the AGENTS.md note).
  4. Console work through APIs — AAB uploads, ko and en store listings, 30 screenshots per app, in-app products, Firebase projects and GA4 properties are all created by scripts. What a person does in the console is only what the APIs do not expose.

Some things the APIs would not do. A new app refused API requests until it had been touched in the console first (the first AAB upload, or granting the service account access), and AdMob's app-creation API is limited-access and returned 403. So AdMob apps and ad units are created in the console, and a script reads their IDs into the config file.

What went wrong?

  • Debug was fine, the release build crashed. The code shrinker R8 removed one constructor, and every release build crashed right at startup. Since then the minified release build is launched twice on a device before every upload (the pre-release checks note).
  • On-device tests ran after submitting for review. End-to-end tests on a Galaxy S21 and S20 on October 4 found nine major defects, five distinct causes. The biggest: if the system killed the app mid-job, the progress screen froze. No crashes and no damaged originals, but the order was backwards. End-to-end tests now come before submission.
  • The test scripts had bugs too. A script that waits for a screen exited with success (0) on timeout, so later checks kept running on the wrong screen. Tools the AI writes for testing need testing too.

If you want to try it

  1. Start with the instruction file — Write down only the rules the agent tends to get wrong, briefly. Keep history elsewhere.
  2. Take the first app all the way — Only after one app reaches a public store page do you see what to automate.
  3. Script the pre-release checks — Make the gate, a release-build launch and an on-device check mandatory before any upload.
  4. Record what was and wasn't verified — In the changelog, write which device checked what, and what was not checked.

Frequently asked questions

Did the AI write all the code?

By commit, 88% carry the AI co-author mark. The person made design decisions, reviewed results, checked on devices and decided on releases. The mark shows collaboration, not a share of lines.

Can one person keep quality up this way?

item.title: How to write AGENTS.md for an AI coding agent – SugarMount
item.description:
AX notes · Measured case

How to write AGENTS.md: only the rules an AI coding agent gets wrong

AGENTS.md is the instruction file an AI coding agent reads before it starts working in a repository. Write down only what the agent tends to get wrong, with the reason, and turn the important rules into tests.

SugarMount shipped four Android apps with one 96-line AGENTS.md, revised 19 times since it was created. The point is not to write a lot.

Examples are taken from the AGENTS.md of SugarMount's app repository (sugar-utils) and shortened, as of October 18, 2026.

What is AGENTS.md?

A Markdown file at the top of the repository. Many AI coding agents read a file by this name as their instructions. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, so SugarMount keeps the same content in both files. Unlike a README, its reader is an agent. An agent reads the repository as if for the first time, every time, so even things a person would remember after hearing once need to be written down.

What goes in?

SectionContentsWhy
What this isThe apps, where each one stands (public on Play, internal testing), stack and SDK levelsSo the agent never guesses that something "shipped"
LayoutOne line per directory: what it ownsSo the same feature is not built twice in different places
Build and testCommands that can be copied and run as isSo the agent does not rediscover how to verify
Rules that are easy to get wrongTwelve of them: the rule, the reason, the scope of any exceptionThe heart of the file
QAEmulator and device test scripts, in orderSo "it builds" is not reported as "done"
Adding the next appThe scaffolding script and what to change by hand afterwardsSo each app does not repeat the same mistakes

What stays out?

  • History — The top of the file says "This file holds current facts only; history goes to CHANGELOG.md." Mix in old versions and the agent reads old rules as current ones.
  • Secrets — Key files get a location and "never commit"; their contents never appear.
  • General advice — The agent already knows "keep the code clean". Keep only what is true of this repository.

How do you write a rule that is easy to get wrong?

Each rule says what not to do, why, and how far any exception reaches. A few of the actual rules:

  1. Identifiers are per app. Package name, ad IDs, Firebase project and billing product live only in the app's config file. Reusing code never means reusing IDs.
  2. Debug uses ad test IDs only; release must not. Both directions are checked.
  3. No user content in analytics or logs. Events have no free-form parameters on purpose, and the file says "never add a Map<String, Any> escape hatch".
  4. Report what was verified on a device versus only compiled. Never describe unshipped features as shipped.

Exceptions are written narrowly. The rule "temp files only in the cache" carries the exception "the document viewer (HWP Viewer SugarDoc) alone keeps a received-documents inbox. Do not fix this back to temp files." Without that sentence, an agent sees the exception as a bug and "fixes" it.

Decisions made by the person carry a date (for example "owner decision 2026-10-05"). The current AGENTS.md has six dated decisions. With a date, an agent can tell which side is newer when it conflicts with an older document.

Enforce rules with checks, not prose

Agents mostly follow instructions, but they can lose track in a long task. So the rules that must never be broken become tests or build checks.

RuleWhat enforces it
Per-app identifiers; no ad test IDs in releaseA ConfigGateTest in every app; release_gate.sh stops the build on PLACEHOLDER or a test ID
No Android dependency in the shared document logicNoAndroidImportsTest
Every string in both Korean and EnglishLint's MissingTranslation and ExtraTranslation raised from warnings to errors
Full-screen ad spacing and capsAdPacerTest; new numbers go into the config with a test, never at a call site
Privacy policy links must be liverelease_gate.sh checks that the policy and support URLs return HTTP 200

The URLs in the last row are this site's per-app privacy policies. Move the site, and app releases stop.

How is it kept up to date?

  1. Add a line where the mistake happened — After a release build of the first app, Compress Image, crashed on launch, a line was added: "run release_launch.sh before every upload", with the reason (which version crashed, and on what).
  2. Change facts in the same commit — When an app goes public or a version moves, AGENTS.md changes in that same commit. Nearly all 19 revisions sit inside feature or release commits.
  3. Move long parts out — Ad policy, design rules and the document viewer design live in their own documents; AGENTS.md keeps only the paths.

Frequently asked questions

How is AGENTS.md different from CLAUDE.md?

Only in which tool reads it. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md; many other agents read AGENTS.md. If the two drift apart, each agent follows different rules, so SugarMount keeps them identical.

How long should it be?

There is no fixed length. The repository that ships SugarMount's four apps uses 96 lines. The longer it gets, the easier it is for an agent to miss an important rule, so move details into other documents and keep the paths.

Can I just use a template?

A template helps with structure, but the file's value is in recording what actually went wrong in your repository. Start short and add a line each time the agent makes a mistake.

item.title: Pre-release checks for an AI-built Android app – SugarMount
item.description:
AX notes · Measured case

What to check before shipping an AI-built Android app: the release gate and an R8 crash

An Android app built with an AI coding agent can run fine as a debug build and still crash the moment its release build starts. So every upload first passes a release gate, a release-build launch check and on-device tests.

On September 23, 2026, the code shrinker R8 removed a single constructor from SugarMount's first app, Compress Image, and every release build crashed at launch. Since then each upload goes through three steps: a release gate, a launch check of the minified release build, and on-device end-to-end tests.

Scripts and numbers come from the code, changelog and on-device QA reports of SugarMount's app repository (sugar-utils), as of October 18, 2026.

Why did it crash when debug was fine?

Debug builds are not shrunk; release builds use R8 to strip code that looks unused. So there are problems that only the release build has, even when every unit test and the debug build pass.

  • Cause — The ads SDK pulls in WorkManager 2.7 and Room 2.2.5. Their keep rule keeps RoomDatabase subclasses but not their constructors. R8 full mode, the default in AGP 9, removed the constructor of WorkDatabase_Impl.
  • Symptom — The app dies right at launch in androidx.startup with "Failed to create an instance of WorkDatabase". The debug build does not reproduce it.
  • Found — By installing and launching the release APK on a real device (Galaxy S23). Until then no release build had been run on a device.
  • Fix — One line in the shared ads module's consumer rules. Room 2.3 and later ship this rule themselves.
-keep class * extends androidx.room.RoomDatabase { <init>(); }

The fix was one line. The lesson was bigger: nothing is verified until the release build has run on a device.

Step 1: what does the release gate stop?

release_gate.sh <app> checks the following in order and builds no AAB if any of them fails.

CheckMistake it stops
Any PLACEHOLDER left in the config fileReleasing a freshly scaffolded app without its IDs
Any AdMob test ID leftShipping test ads (zero revenue)
Firebase config file presentA release without analytics and crash reports
Privacy policy and support URLs return HTTP 200A 404 behind the policy link in Settings or on the store listing (a policy problem)
Tests of the gate rules themselvesA broken check that silently stops nothing
Release config check, release unit tests, lint, AAB buildConfig and translation gaps that exist only in the release variant

HWP Viewer SugarDoc, which has no ads, is checked the other way round: the build fails if an ads SDK enters the release dependencies or an advertising ID permission is merged into the manifest.

Step 2: launch the minified release build twice

release_launch.sh <app> <device> installs the R8-shrunk release APK, force-stops the app and cold-starts it twice. After each launch it counts only this package's lines in the crash log since that moment, and checks that the process is alive.

  • It never clears logcat, so it works on a phone other people use too; other apps' crashes are not counted.
  • If reading logcat fails, the check fails. It never turns into "no crash".
  • The rule to run it before every upload is also written in the agent instruction file (the AGENTS.md note).

Step 3: what did on-device end-to-end tests find?

Results for the three photo apps on a Galaxy S21 (Android 15), October 4, 2026, scenario by scenario:

AppPassed / failed / skipped
Compress Image24 / 2 / 2
Flip & Rotate Image25 / 4 / 1
Convert Image22 / 3 / 2

No crashes and no damaged originals; the minified release builds of all three launched cleanly both times. But there were nine major defects with five distinct causes. The biggest, shared by all three apps: if the system killed the app mid-job, the progress screen froze at 0 / 0. Neither the emulator nor the unit tests had shown it.

These tests ran after the apps had been submitted for production review. Wrong order. Now end-to-end tests come before submission; after the fixes, 410 unit tests, lint and all three release gates passed again before release.

When you let AI run the checks

  • "It builds" is not "done". Agents tend to report completion once code compiles. Make them report which device checked what, and what was not checked.
  • Test the test tools. A script that waits for a screen once exited with success on timeout, so later checks ran on the wrong screen. It now fails on timeout.
  • Verify with a different agent. In on-device QA, three per-app agents found defects and a fourth reproduced each one with its own screenshots and traced the cause in the code. Whoever built it misses things when checking their own work.

Frequently asked questions

Can you catch R8 problems in advance?

The surest way is to actually launch a build shrunk with the release settings on a device. Debug builds and unit tests never go through shrinking, so they cannot catch a missing keep rule.

Is an emulator enough?

It was not. State loss after process death, and "keep original name" failing because of the file names the photo picker hands over, showed up only in on-device tests. Use the emulator for quick checks and a real device before release.

Are the gate scripts public?

The repository is private. The table above lists every check shared by all apps, so you can build the same thing in the same order. The HWP viewer adds checks that compare its document engine files and fonts against pinned sources.

Data and permissions

  • The app receives only the photos you pick in the Android photo picker. It does not ask for access to all your storage.
  • Compression, resizing, previews and saving all happen on your device. Photos, results and file names are never sent to a server or third party. Processing needs no internet connection.
  • Originals are never modified or deleted. Results become new files when you save them.
  • Anonymous usage stats (Firebase / Google Analytics) and crash reports (Firebase Crashlytics) are on by default. Turn each off in Settings under “Send anonymous usage stats” and “Send crash reports”. Neither includes photos or file names.
  • The free version shows Google AdMob ads. The ads SDK may process data such as the advertising ID under Google’s policies; change your consent in Settings under “Ad privacy options”.
  • Internet access is used for ads, the Pro purchase, and sending stats and crash reports. There is no account or sign-in.

Details are in the Compress Image privacy policy.

Free and Pro

Free

  • All three modes
  • Up to 20 photos per batch
  • Shows ads

Pro

  • One-time purchase, not a subscription
  • No ads
  • Up to 100 photos per batch

The price is shown on the Google Play purchase screen. On a new device, use “Restore purchase” in Settings to apply a purchase made with the same Google account.

What it cannot do

  • Results are saved as JPEG only. Transparent areas in PNG or WebP are filled with white, and animated images are not supported.
  • Photos are never enlarged. A very low limit may be out of reach; the app tells you when it is.
  • PNG, WebP and HEIC photos can grow when converted to JPEG. The app then marks them “larger than the original”.

FAQ

How do I get a photo under 500 KB?

Pick the photo, choose 500 KB under “Fit to size” and tap “Create results”. The limit applies to each photo, and 1 KB is counted as 1000 bytes.

Does the app change or delete my original photos?

No. Originals stay as they are; results are saved as new files in the Pictures/SugarCompress folder.

What happens to a JPEG that is already small?

A JPEG result is never larger than the original. If the photo is already small enough, it is kept at original quality without recompressing, with only location and camera info removed.

Does it work offline?

Yes. Photos are processed on your device, so no connection is needed. Only ads and the Pro purchase need the internet.
